window: TKE D - Serve deployment, health and URL
scope: Serve-owned TKE execution and access adapter inside the existing ServeRuntimeAdapter/ServeAccessControl contracts. No production access, deployment, purchase, deletion or charge. Real TKE, ingress, certificate and browser routing are not run.

source.workingTree: shared uncommitted worktree; the serve domain diff below is the reviewed change

serve_owned_tke_execution_adapter.boundary: the installation Agent execution boundary reached over the scoped, signed /fabric/workspace-application-runtimes capability; read-only for resources
fixes: a gateway-published entry (serviceName + port) is no longer read as Entry.URL; Serve resolves the publishable origin from the installation-declared RouteOrigin (OPL_PUBLIC_URL scheme, OPL_WORKSPACE_APPLICATION_DOMAIN per-binding origin, OPL_WORKSPACE_DOMAIN retained /w/<workspaceId>/ entry) and refuses when none is declared instead of guessing a host
the in-cluster upstream is validated as exactly one DNS label plus the declared port; an address, localhost or a compound name is refused
model configuration (ModelSelections and ModelConfigurationVersion) is delivered instead of rejected
readiness requires the provider's whole-runtime status ready AND every declared component observed ready AND a resolved publishable entry; a Pod phase or a persisted pointer is never readiness
the readiness evidence identity binds the runtime operation, resolved origin, validated upstream, whole-runtime observation and applied model configuration version

serve_access_control.type: delivery.Service implements api.ServeAccessControl over serve.access_bindings and serve.access_switches
fixes: provider conditional-revision CAS: only a confirmed provider readback advances the route generation (fence preserves it, activate/rollback advance it by exactly one)
persistent execution epoch per binding; an older epoch is refused with STALE_EXECUTION_EPOCH
one unresolved switch per binding blocks every new switch (lost ACK stays unknown until the original provider command is read back)
activation requires the target deployment's own ready runtime instance with the presented readiness receipt and a confirmed fence for its epoch
rollback requires the original confirmed switch and a provider-confirmed revision

RouteProvider port: when no installation route provider is configured Serve records the exact switch it committed to and refuses with route_provider_unavailable instead of reporting an activated route

serve_runtime_adapter.note: executes/observes the exact original command through the configured TKE adapter and the Fabric-confirmed resource binding; persists nothing, so it cannot become a second delivery writer

implemented.registration: delivery.Service.Register now exposes ServeRuntimeAdapter and ServeAccessControl alongside ServeProductService and ServeAgentCoordination

commands.environment: no database DSN; PostgreSQL-backed tests skipped
isolated local docker PostgreSQL 16 (tke-d-serve-pg), serve migration installed by the real migration entrypoint; NOT production

evidence.entry_to_url: the provider fixture reports serviceName app-runtime-http-main and port 8080; Serve publishes https://<workspaceId>-<sha1 label>.apps.example/ and refuses with no declared origin; the label ws-route-62097bae4a90 was recomputed independently with SHA-1 over ('workspace-application-origin','ws-route','knowledge-app')
evidence.ready_vs_running: a fixture whose component is pending yields STARTING with no address; a failed component yields FAILED with no address; only all-components-ready plus a resolved entry yields READY with readiness evidence
evidence.lost_ack_and_epoch_fencing: a provider transport failure leaves the switch unknown and blocks the next switch (route_switch_unresolved); ObserveRoute reads back the original switch by its provider command id; an older execution epoch is refused with stale_execution_epoch
evidence.single_current: one route binding per workspace (UNIQUE workspace_id) asserted after fence+activate; the confirmed switch id is committed on the deployment
evidence.secret_not_rejected_silently: a command carrying a Secret binding is refused with credential_injection_wire_missing and the provider is never called; the fixture asserts no Secret material ever travels in the execution input

shared_contract_gap.summary: An application that needs an injected Secret or platform-issued credential cannot be executed: Serve holds only an opaque Secret binding identity, and no field on the delivery wire transports the Secret delivery reference the execution boundary injects.

rpc_field_caller_counterexample.missing_field: a typed runtime configuration carrying the Secret delivery reference(s) and non-secret runtime configuration, e.g. `WorkspaceApplicationRuntimeConfiguration runtime_configuration = 16` with entries `{name, secretRef, version, key}` and `{name, target, env}`; the execution boundary's own input type `contracts.WorkspaceApplicationRuntimeInput` already accepts `configuration` + `secretBindings`, so no new execution model is needed
rpc_field_caller_counterexample.caller: services/workspace/internal/launch/runtime.go (builds RuntimeDeployCommand; the accepted quote supplies model selections)
rpc_field_caller_counterexample.owner_that_must_produce_the_reference: the Gateway secret owner (legacy Control Plane produced it through workspaceOPLApplicationConfiguration -> SyncWorkspaceGatewaySecretByID returning {SecretRef, Version}; target owner is GatewayCoordination.CreateManagedKey -> ManagedKeyBinding.secret_delivery_reference plus FabricCoordination.BindSecret)
rpc_field_caller_counterexample.counterexample: revision declares secretInputs[{name:'gateway', target:'/run/secrets/opl_gateway_api_key', env:'OPL_GATEWAY_API_KEY_FILE'}] and credentials[{kind:'gateway_key'}]; the command sets secret_binding_id; currently refused as credential_injection_wire_missing. Executing without the reference would start an Agent that cannot reach any model, so it is never silently degraded.
legacy_migration_input: services/control-plane/internal/server/workspace_application_origin.go: retained per-binding origin and /w/<workspaceId>/ entry semantics reproduced by Serve's RouteOrigin

shared_contract_gap.not_invented: no new shared DTO, no simplified deployment model, no packages/contracts change; the exact field/caller/counterexample is handed to the coordinator

not_run: real Tencent TKE cluster execution, ingress publication, certificate and DNS
HTML/static/API/SSE routing through a real gateway and tenant isolation over a live origin
ServeRuntimeAdapter.StopRuntime / ReloadRuntime / ReadApplicationCredentials (no installation path in this slice)
the ServeAccessControl to Deploy orchestration and the old caller/writer switch (W01 contracts and the coordinator's serial caller migration)
W01 default App application contracts (runtime_release provenance / application union)
notes: the previous Serve session worktree codex/serve-deployment-clean was read only as migration input; its wire changes were not copied and no old credential was reused
the adapter is Serve-owned: Fabric is reached as the resource/execution provider over the existing admitted capability and is never asked to own Agent readiness or routing
